chunks: Abu Ahmad al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abdawayh al-Sarraj al-Zahid al-Hamdani, in Hamdan, told us, saying: Abu Amr Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Amrun told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Na'is al-Baghdadi told us, saying: Ibn al-Humani told us, saying: 'Abd al-Salam told us, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Farwa, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Huraira, who said:

The 'Badal' (exchange) in the Jahiliyyah was that a man would say to another man: 'Exchange me with your wife and I will exchange you with my wife; you step down for me from your wife, and I step down for you from my wife.' Then Allah, Exalted and Glorious, sent down: 'Nor (is it) for you to exchange them for (other) wives, even if their beauty impress you.'

He said: 'Uyayna ibn Hassn entered upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family), and with him was Aisha, and he entered without permission. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) said to him: 'And where is your request for permission?' He said: 'I have not sought permission from a man from Mudar since I reached maturity.' Then he said: 'Who is this Humaira [the red-skinned one] next to you?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: 'This is Aisha, the Mother of the Believers.' 'Uyayna said: 'Shall I not step down for you from the best of creation, and you step down for me from her?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious, has forbidden that for me.'
When he left, Aisha said to him: 'Who is this, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'This is a fool that is obeyed, and indeed, as you see, he is the master of his people.'

key_terms.أُمُّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Mother of the Believers (title for the Prophet's wives)
key_terms.الْبَدَلُ: Exchange (specifically of wives in pre-Islamic times)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Badal' in marriage and how did 'Uyayna ibn Hassn interact with the Prophet?
ai.summary: This narration from *Mani al-Akhbar* elucidates the pre-Islamic custom of *Badal* (wife exchange) and its abrogation by the Quranic verse 33:52, while also illustrating the Prophet’s unique marital privileges. The incident with 'Uyayna ibn Hassn serves as a practical demonstration of this prohibition, where the Prophet clarifies that the divine ban applies specifically to him, distinguishing his status from the general community. The concluding description of 'Uyayna as a 'fool who is obeyed' reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of his tribal authority and political influence despite his perceived lack of religious insight.
